'''Johanna Maria Henrica (Anneke) Levelt Sengers''' (4 March 1929 – 28 February 2024) was a Dutch physicist known for her work on [[Critical point (thermodynamics)|critical states]] of [[fluid]]s. She retired from the [[National Institute of Standards and Technology]] (NIST) in 1994, after a 31 year career there.<ref name="profile">{{citation|url=http://www.boulder.nist.gov/div838/ProfilesSengers.html|title=Johanna M.H. Anneke Levelt Sengers (Scientist Emeritus)|work=Selected Employee Profiles|publisher=[[National Institute of Standards and Technology]] Chemical Science and Technology Laboratory, Thermophysical Properties Division|access-date=29 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304122301/http://www.boulder.nist.gov/div838/ProfilesSengers.html|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead}}.</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nist.gov/mml/csd/johanna-mh-levelt-sengers-curriculum-vitae |website=nist.gov |access-date=10 March 2024 |title=Johanna M.H. Levelt Sengers Curriculum Vitae |date=November 15, 2019 |publisher=National Institute of Standards and Technology}}</ref> In 2005 Levelt Sengers was co-chair (with [[Manju Sharma (biologist)|Dr Manju Sharma]]) for the InterAcademy Council of the advisory report 'Women for Science' published June 2006. She co-chaired the [[InterAmerican Network of Academies of Sciences]] women for science program.<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.ianas.org/women.html|title=Women for Science|publisher=InterAmerican Network of Academies of Sciences|access-date=29 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151024165119/http://www.ianas.org/women.html|archive-date=24 October 2015|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

==Education and career==
Levelt Sengers was born on 4 March 1929<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gPGZJ_YuMwgC&q=Johanna+Levelt+Sengers+birth+date&pg=PA614|title=American Women of Science Since 1900: Essays A-H|volume=1|pages=614|author=Tiffany K. Wayne|publisher=Greenwood publishing group|year=2011|isbn=978-1-59884-158-9}}</ref> in Amsterdam,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.stamboomplus.com/index.php?option=com_sengers&task=spo&ww=sp/416053A.PDF |title=The Sengers Family Tree, Stamboom.Johanna Maria Henrica Levelt |website=www.stamboomplus.com |access-date=10 March 2024 |publisher=Chris Sengers |first=Chris |last=Sengers}}</ref> Netherlands.<ref name="pai">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ipst.umd.edu/flyers/pai2014brochure.pdf |title=20th Annual Shih-I Pai Lecture, Johanna M. H. (Anneke) Levelt Sengers, Scientist Emeritus National Institute of Standards and Technology, TUESDAY, OCTOBER 7, 2014, "Pride and Prejudice in Science and Engineering" |archive-date=21 November 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141121215158/http://www.ipst.umd.edu/flyers/pai2014brochure.pdf |access-date=10 March 2024}}</ref> Her father was a chemist and her mother had studied physics. She was the eldest child and had nine siblings. During World War II her father spent time in [[Buchenwald concentration camp]].<ref name="vdheijden">{{cite news |last1=van der Heijden |first1=Margriet |url=https://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2024/03/05/anneke-levelt-sengers-1929-2024-a4192117 |url-access=subscription |title=Anneke Levelt Sengers (1929–2024) |newspaper=NRC |language=nl |publisher=NRC Handelsblad |date=5 March 2024 |access-date=9 March 2024}}</ref>

Levelt Sengers started studying physics at the [[University of Amsterdam]] in 1947.<ref name="vdheijden"/> She earned her ''candidaats'' (Bachelor of Science)<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20161119193330/http://www.nist.gov/mml/csd/levelt-sengers.cfm|title=Johanna M. Levelt-Sengers}} The National Institute of Standards and Technology</ref> in physics and chemistry from the [[University of Amsterdam]] in 1950, a Master of Science there in 1954 and completed her Ph.D. from the same university in 1958. Her dissertation, ''Measurements of the Compressibility of Argon in the Gaseous and Liquid Phase'', was jointly promoted by {{ill|Antonius M. J. F. Michels|nl|Antonius Mathias Johannes Friedrich Michels}} and {{ill|Jan de Boer (1911–2010)|lt=Jan de Boer|nl|Jan de Boer (1911-2010)}}.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=115358}}</ref>

She emigrated to the United States in 1963 and joined the [[National Bureau of Standards]] (later renamed to NIST).<ref name="pai"/>

==Awards and honors==
In 1990, Levelt Sengers became a corresponding member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|author= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160130210434/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/correspondents/4465?set_language=en |archive-date=2016-01-30 |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/correspondents/4465?set_language=en |title=Johanna Levelt Sengers |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |access-date=10 March 2024}}</ref> In 1992, [[Delft University of Technology]] gave her an honorary doctorate.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tudelft.nl/over-tu-delft/organisatie/hoogleraren/eredoctoraten |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240305175329/https://www.tudelft.nl/over-tu-delft/organisatie/hoogleraren/eredoctoraten |title=Eredoctoraten |language=nl |publisher=Delft University of Technology |date= |archive-date=5 March 2024}}</ref> She was a [[fellow]] of the [[American Society of Mechanical Engineers]], the [[American Physical Society]], and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]],<ref name="profile"/> and a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] and [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="chemnews"/>
She was the [[L'Oréal-UNESCO Awards for Women in Science|L'Oréal-UNESCO Award for Women in Science]] 2003 Laureate for North America,<ref name="chemnews">{{citation|url=http://pubs.acs.org/cen/awards/8113/8113awards2.html|title=Levelt Sengers Garners L'Oréal UNESCO Award|magazine=Chemical & Engineering News|date=31 March 2003|volume=81|issue=13|page=47|publisher=[[American Chemical Society]]}}.</ref> and the 2006 winner of the ASME [[Yeram S. Touloukian]] Award.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.asme.org/about-asme/participate/honors-awards/achievement-awards/yeram-s-touloukian-award|title=Yeram S. Touloukian Award|journal=International Journal of Thermophysics|volume=9|issue=5|pages=631–633|access-date=29 October 2015|bibcode=  1988IJT.....9..631.|year=1988|doi=10.1007/BF00503231|s2cid=189901752}}.</ref> In 2015, the IANAS Women for Science Program announced an award for young women scientists would be named the Anneke Levelt-Senger Prize (sic) in her honor.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://u.tt/index.php?articles=1&article_key=4525&wk=11 | title=The University of Trinidad and Tobago - School of Postgraduate Studies, Research and Development | publisher=The University of Trinidad and Tobago | date=19 October 2015 | access-date=30 October 2015}}</ref>

==Personal life and death==
Anneke Levelt Sengers married physicist [[Jan V. Sengers]] in 1962; their four children include computer scientist and ethnographer [[Phoebe Sengers]].<ref name="vdheijden"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://eng.umd.edu/html/media/e-at-m/03_e@m_fall.pdf|publisher=University of Maryland|title=Forward thinking|work=Engineering @ Maryland|date=Fall 2003|page=31}}</ref> In 1975 she and her husband became naturalized US citizens.<ref name="vdheijden"/>

Levelt Sengers died on 28 February 2024, a week shy of her 95th birthday.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Obituary information for J.M.H. "Anneke" Levelt Sengers |url=https://www.devolfuneralhome.com/obituaries/JMH-Anneke-Levelt-Sengers?obId=30921314 |access-date=5 March 2024 |website=www.devolfuneralhome.com}}</ref>
